claim: *Modeling and enforcement are separate decisions.* The measurement model defines the quantity and reference bound; Alignment determines whether the result is observed, used to adapt behavior, used to trigger graceful degradation, or enforced by a gate.

topology.description: Separate measurement modeling and enforcement decisions over one shared model; four equal choices.

required_terms: Model: what quantity and bound matter? Alignment: what enforcement is justified?
bw_encoding: Black outlines and arrows; white nodes; sparse 3–7% gray groups. Every non-solid relation is locally labeled; no distinction depends on color.
redesign: Native semantic redraw; colors replaced by labeled relations and line conventions.
alt: A quantity and reference bound are compared in the modeling stage. The enforcement stage uses that same model and branches to four peer choices: observe, adapt, degrade or gate. Modeling names what matters; enforcement chooses its force. The candidate uses black lines, white backgrounds and sparse gray; meaning does not depend on color.
